name: Malai Kofta

ingredients.name: Cornflour (corn starch)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 2 tsp (1 tsp in the mix, 1 tsp for coating)

ingredients.name: Sunflower or groundnut oil, for deep-frying
ingredients.householdMeasure: about 1 cup in the kadai; about 2 tsp absorbed

ingredients.name: Hot water, for soaking the cashews
Fresh cream (malai), about 25% fat (e.g. Amul fresh cream)

equipment: Small saucepan or pressure cooker, for boiling the potato
Small heavy kadai (about 18 cm), for deep-frying
Slotted spoon (jhara) and a plate lined with paper towel
Grater (for potato, paneer, ginger and garlic)
Mixer-grinder with a small (chutney) jar, for the cashew paste and the onion-tomato purée
Second pan or kadai with a lid, for the gravy (non-stick or heavy steel)
Measuring spoons and a measuring cup (a normal teaspoon and a steel glass are fine stand-ins)

steps.title: Soak the cashews
steps.text: Put 8 cashews (12 g) in a small bowl and pour 60 ml (¼ cup) hot water over them. Leave them while you make the koftas.
steps.tip: Keep the soaking water; it goes into the paste.
steps.visualCue: Cashews fully under water
steps.videoShot: Hot water being poured over cashews in a steel bowl.

steps.title: Boil the potato
steps.text: Put 1 small potato (about 45 g) in a pressure cooker with ½ cup water and cook for 2 whistles on medium (or boil covered in a saucepan for 15–18 min).
steps.tip: Do not over-boil; a watery potato makes koftas that fall apart in the oil.
steps.visualCue: A knife slides into the centre with no resistance, but the potato is not split or waterlogged
steps.cameraCheck: The knife in the boiled potato
steps.videoShot: A knife sliding cleanly into a boiled potato.

steps.title: Peel and cool the potato
steps.text: Peel it and let it cool completely on a plate.
steps.visualCue: Dry surface, no steam rising
steps.cameraCheck: The peeled potato on the plate
steps.videoShot: The skin peeling away from a warm potato.

steps.title: Grate the potato
steps.text: Grate the cooled potato into the mixing bowl (35 g).
steps.visualCue: Fine, fluffy, lump-free shreds
steps.cameraCheck: The grated potato in the bowl
steps.videoShot: Potato being rubbed on the fine side of a grater.

steps.title: Grate the paneer
steps.text: Grate 40 g paneer into the same bowl.
steps.tip: If the paneer is wet, squeeze it in a cloth first; dry paneer holds better.
steps.visualCue: Soft white crumbs, no big lumps
steps.cameraCheck: Paneer and potato in the bowl
steps.videoShot: Paneer block being grated over the bowl.

steps.title: Add the binder and seasoning
steps.text: Add 1 tsp (3 g) cornflour, a pinch of salt (0.5 g) and a small pinch of garam masala.
steps.visualCue: White powder on top of the mix
steps.cameraCheck: The bowl with cornflour on top
steps.videoShot: A teaspoon of cornflour tipping into the bowl.

steps.title: Knead the mix
steps.text: Knead with your palm for about 1–2 minutes into a smooth, soft dough.
steps.tip: Sticky? Add ½ tsp more cornflour. Crumbly? Add 1 tsp more grated paneer.
steps.visualCue: A smooth ball that does not stick to your hand and shows no cracks when pressed
steps.cameraCheck: The dough ball in your palm
steps.videoShot: The heel of the hand pressing the mix smooth.

steps.title: Make the stuffing
steps.text: Finely chop 2 cashews (3 g) and mix them with 4 raisins (2 g).
steps.visualCue: Tiny cashew bits with whole raisins
steps.videoShot: A knife chopping cashews into bits.

steps.title: Divide the dough
steps.text: Divide the dough into 3 equal portions (about 26 g each).
steps.visualCue: Three lumps the same size
steps.videoShot: The dough pinched into three.

steps.title: Stuff and shape the koftas
steps.text: Flatten one portion in your palm, place a third of the stuffing in the middle, close the edges, and roll it into a smooth ball. Repeat for all 3.
steps.tip: Grease your palms with a drop of oil if the dough sticks; seal any crack, or the kofta will open in the oil.
steps.visualCue: Smooth, crack-free balls about the size of a lime, with no stuffing showing
steps.videoShot: Palms rolling a stuffed ball smooth.

steps.title: Coat the koftas
steps.text: Spread the remaining 1 tsp (3 g) cornflour on a plate and roll each kofta in it, then tap off the excess.
steps.visualCue: A thin, even white dusting
steps.videoShot: A kofta rolling through cornflour.

steps.title: Heat the frying oil
steps.text: Pour about 250 ml oil into the small kadai and heat on medium to about 170–180 °C.
steps.tip: Cold oil makes the koftas soak up oil and break; smoking oil browns the outside before the inside heats.
steps.visualCue: A pea-sized bit of dough dropped in rises in 2–3 seconds with steady bubbles (not instantly with violent bubbling, which is too hot)
steps.cameraCheck: The oil test with the bit of dough
steps.videoShot: A tiny ball of dough rising and sizzling.

steps.title: Test-fry one kofta
steps.text: Slide 1 kofta gently into the oil with a spoon. Do not touch it for the first 30 seconds.
steps.tip: If it starts to crack, take it out, knead ½ tsp cornflour into the remaining two, and re-coat.
steps.visualCue: The kofta stays whole and bubbles gently around it
steps.cameraCheck: The first kofta in the oil
steps.videoShot: One kofta lowered into the oil.

steps.title: Fry all the koftas
steps.text: Add the other 2 koftas and fry on medium heat, turning gently every 30–40 seconds.
steps.visualCue: Evenly golden-brown all over with a crisp crust
steps.cameraCheck: The golden koftas in the kadai
steps.videoShot: The slotted spoon rolling the koftas.

steps.title: Drain the koftas
steps.text: Lift them out with the slotted spoon onto the paper-lined plate. Turn off the frying oil.
steps.tip: Let the leftover oil cool, strain it and reuse it once for frying; do not reheat it many times.
steps.visualCue: Golden balls, paper showing light oil spots
steps.cameraCheck: The 3 fried koftas on the paper
steps.videoShot: Koftas lifted out, oil dripping back.

steps.title: Chop the onion
steps.text: Roughly chop ½ medium onion (50 g).
steps.visualCue: Rough chunks, about ⅓ cup
steps.videoShot: Knife cutting onion into chunks.

steps.title: Grate the ginger and garlic
steps.text: Grate ¼-inch ginger (3 g) and 1 large garlic clove (3 g).
steps.visualCue: A small heap of pale, wet paste
steps.videoShot: Ginger rubbed on the grater.

steps.title: Chop the tomato
steps.text: Roughly chop 1 small-medium tomato (80 g).
steps.visualCue: Juicy red chunks, about ½ cup
steps.videoShot: Tomato cut into chunks.

steps.title: Grind the cashew paste
steps.text: Put the soaked cashews and their water in the small mixer jar and grind until completely smooth. Set aside.
steps.visualCue: A smooth, pourable, off-white paste with no grit when rubbed between fingers
steps.videoShot: The mixer jar opening to show a silky paste.

steps.title: Heat the oil and butter
steps.text: Put the gravy pan on medium heat and add 1 tsp (5 ml) oil and 1 tsp (5 g) butter.
steps.visualCue: Butter melted and foaming lightly
steps.videoShot: Butter melting into oil.

steps.title: Temper the whole spices
steps.text: Add 1 bay leaf, 1 crushed cardamom pod and ¼ tsp cumin seeds.
steps.tip: Butter burns faster than oil; keep the heat at medium.
steps.visualCue: Cumin sizzles and darkens one shade; nutty smell
steps.videoShot: Cumin crackling in the fat.

steps.title: Cook the onion
steps.text: Add the chopped onion and stir on medium heat.
steps.visualCue: Soft, translucent, just turning light golden at the edges (not brown; malai kofta gravy should stay pale orange)
steps.videoShot: Spatula turning translucent onion.

steps.title: Add the ginger and garlic
steps.text: Stir in the grated ginger-garlic.
steps.visualCue: The raw garlic smell goes
steps.videoShot: The paste stirred in.

steps.title: Add the tomato and salt
steps.text: Add the chopped tomato and 1.5 g (¼ tsp) salt. Stir.
steps.visualCue: Red tomato through the onion
steps.videoShot: Tomato tipping into the pan.

steps.title: Cook the tomato soft
steps.text: Cover and cook on medium-low, stirring twice.
steps.visualCue: Tomato mushy and the skins loosening
steps.cameraCheck: The mushy tomato-onion with the lid lifted
steps.videoShot: The spatula mashing soft tomato.

steps.title: Blend the masala
steps.text: Turn off the heat, take out the bay leaf, cool 2 minutes, then blend the onion-tomato mix to a smooth purée (use the same mixer jar; no need to wash it).
steps.tip: Let it cool slightly first; hot liquid can push the mixer lid off.
steps.visualCue: A smooth orange-red purée
steps.videoShot: The jar pouring purée back into the pan.

steps.title: Cook the purée with the powders
steps.text: Pour the purée back into the pan on low-medium heat and add ½ tsp Kashmiri chilli powder, ½ tsp coriander powder and a pinch of turmeric. Stir.
steps.visualCue: The purée darkens slightly and thickens; no raw-powder smell
steps.videoShot: Powders stirred into the bubbling purée.

steps.title: Add the cashew paste
steps.text: Stir in the cashew paste and cook on low, stirring all the time.
steps.tip: Cashew paste catches quickly on the bottom; keep stirring and keep the heat low.
steps.visualCue: A thick, glossy gravy with tiny oil drops at the edges
steps.videoShot: Close-up of the glossy gravy.

steps.title: Add water and sugar
steps.text: Pour in 100 ml water and ½ tsp (2 g) sugar. Stir and simmer on low.
steps.visualCue: Gravy about as thick as pouring custard and coats the back of the spoon
steps.videoShot: A finger line drawn through gravy on the spoon.

steps.title: Taste the gravy
steps.text: Taste and add a pinch more salt only if needed.
steps.visualCue: Mildly sweet, creamy, gently spiced
steps.videoShot: A spoon lifted for tasting.

steps.title: Add the cream
steps.text: Lower the heat to the minimum and stir in 20 ml (4 tsp) fresh cream.
steps.visualCue: Lighter, creamy orange colour; gravy just steams (do not boil hard, or the cream can split)
steps.videoShot: Cream poured in a circle and stirred.

steps.title: Finish the gravy
steps.text: Crush ½ tsp kasuri methi between your palms over the pan, add ¼ tsp garam masala, stir, and turn off the heat.
steps.visualCue: Green flecks and a warm, sweet smell
steps.cameraCheck: The kasuri methi on the gravy
steps.videoShot: Palms rubbing kasuri methi over the pan.

steps.title: Place the koftas in the bowl
steps.text: Put the 3 fried koftas in a serving bowl.
steps.tip: Do not simmer the koftas in the gravy; they soften and fall apart within minutes.
steps.visualCue: Three golden balls in an empty bowl
steps.videoShot: Koftas placed in a bowl one by one.

steps.title: Pour the gravy and serve
steps.text: Pour the hot gravy over the koftas just before eating and scatter 2 tsp chopped coriander leaves on top.
steps.visualCue: Koftas half-covered in glossy orange gravy, green garnish
steps.videoShot: Gravy ladled over the koftas, steam rising.

reasons: paneer and cashew give about 13 g protein plus good calcium and phosphorus, the gravy has real tomato and onion, and the home version uses measured fat (about 2 tsp absorbed frying oil, 1 tsp oil, 1 tsp butter, 4 tsp cream). But the koftas are deep-fried, about two-thirds of the calories come from fat, saturated fat is about 13 g (over half the daily limit) and sodium is about 835 mg, with little fibre or vegetable. Restaurant versions commonly use more cream, butter and khoya, sweeter gravy, more salt, often reused frying oil, and come with butter naan.

researchRating.basis: malai kofta is one of the best-known "party" and restaurant vegetarian curries in India and on Indian menus abroad. Hebbar's Kitchen's malai kofta shows 4.99 from 315 votes, Tarla Dalal's creamy kofta curry 5.0 (6 reviews), Veg Recipes of India's restaurant-style recipe has at least 8 pages of reader comments, and it is published by Indian Healthy Recipes, Cook Click n Devour, Archana's Kitchen, Sanjeev Kapoor and Ranveer Brar, with many vegan and Jain versions. Points come off because it is heavy, some find the sweet gravy cloying, and koftas breaking in the oil is a frequent home-cook complaint.

storage: Store the koftas and gravy separately. The gravy keeps 2 days in the fridge in a closed box (cool within 1 hour) and freezes for up to 1 month. Fried koftas keep 1 day in the fridge or up to 1 month frozen in an airtight box. Reheat the gravy in a pan on low with 2–3 tbsp water, stirring, until it just bubbles (it thickens in the fridge); reheat the koftas in an air fryer or oven at 180 °C for 5–6 min (or in a dry pan, covered, turning) so they crisp again; microwaving makes them soft. Koftas already soaked in gravy turn mushy, so do not store them together.
leftoverRemix: Kofta kathi roll. Halve the leftover koftas, warm them in a dry pan, and boil down the leftover gravy until it is thick enough to spread. Spread the gravy on a hot roti or paratha, lay the kofta halves on it, top with sliced onion, a squeeze of lemon, chaat masala and green chutney, and roll it tight. The creamy gravy works like a sauce in a Mumbai-style frankie.
burnOff: about 7.3 km of running (510 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 10.2 km of brisk walking (about 2 hours at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.). With 1 butter naan (about 810 kcal): about 11.6 km running or 16.2 km walking (est.).

navratri.reason: paneer and potato are allowed, but swap cornflour for singhara or rajgira flour, skip onion, garlic, turmeric, coriander powder and garam masala, and use sendha namak (common vrat rule set, Veg Recipes of India; it lists a vrat aloo-paneer kofta made with fasting flours).

ekadashi.reason: same swaps as Navratri; cornflour (maize) is a grain avoided on Ekadashi in the most common rule set.

jain.reason: potato, onion, garlic and fresh ginger are root vegetables; use raw banana and the onion-free tomato-cashew gravy.

ramadan.reason: vegetarian, so no halal-meat issue; it is rich and heavy, so it suits the iftar dinner better than sehri.

jain.reason: swap potato for raw banana, skip onion and garlic, and use dry ginger powder (sonth) instead of fresh ginger (see Jain variant).

vegan.reason: paneer to pressed firm tofu, butter to oil and fresh cream to cashew cream (see Vegan variant).

pescatarian.reason: vegetarian, no meat, so it fits a pescatarian diet.

sattvik.reason: skip the onion and garlic and build the gravy on tomato and cashew (the Jain variant's gravy works; potato can stay).

glutenFree.reason: the binder is cornflour (maize starch), not maida, and the main recipe uses no hing; check the cornflour pack says pure maize starch, as some recipes and blends use maida or wheat-based "corn flour".

dairyFree.reason: contains paneer, butter and fresh cream; use the Vegan variant.

description: A rich vegetarian, gluten-free North Indian curry of fried paneer-potato koftas in cashew-cream gravy; Jain, vegan and low-oil versions below.
